storylines.name: Use spatial planning to steer shared landscapes
storylines.description: A strong pattern recurs in which land-use zoning, siting controls, basin planning, and use of existing infrastructure align with conservation, climate, water, agriculture, fisheries, and minerals objectives. This tends to work through practical screening of sensitive areas such as wetlands, upper watersheds, reserves, scenic areas, and cultivated land before development or sector expansion proceeds.

storylines.name: Reinforce catchment management across land and water
storylines.description: Catchment and watershed stewardship recurs as a shared delivery mechanism linking soil protection, erosion control, wetland retention, aquifer protection, river-basin planning, and water quality management. The evidence points to land restoration and water governance reinforcing each other through sediment reduction, infiltration, recharge protection, and resilience in upper watersheds and river systems.

storylines.name: Carry environmental safeguards through sector modernization
storylines.description: Across several pairings, modernization measures such as extension, standards, traceability, monitoring, regulation, rehabilitation, and data sharing align with biodiversity, climate, land, and water goals. This recurs in agriculture, fisheries, and minerals where governance tools and compliance systems provide channels for eco-friendly production, pollution control, restoration, and risk management.

storylines.name: Review land competition from expansion measures
storylines.description: A recurring friction is flagged for review where agricultural growth, mineral zoning, infrastructure, settlement expansion, or development of high-potential locations may draw on the same land base targeted for forests, wetlands, restoration, cultivated land protection, or biodiversity coverage. The mechanism is usually spatial overlap in sensitive or multi-use areas rather than a settled goal conflict.

storylines.name: Review water demand from production growth
storylines.description: Possible misalignment recurs where cropping expansion, irrigation rehabilitation, aquaculture growth, agro-industrial activity, mining, or energy and industrial siting could increase pressure on finite surface water, groundwater, wetlands, and basin allocation systems. The evidence tends to point to shared concerns around water quantity, water quality, recharge zones, and competing users in the same basins.

storylines.name: Review ecosystem pressures from fisheries expansion
storylines.description: Another storyline recurs around fisheries and aquaculture growth being flagged for review where export-oriented production, pond siting, marine expansion, or exotic species introduction may affect wetlands, inland waters, coastal habitats, biodiversity safeguards, or climate-sensitive aquatic areas. The friction tends to arise in shared aquatic spaces through siting, habitat pressure, biosecurity, and water quality pathways.

summary_paragraph: Across Sri Lanka's policy set, reinforcement appears more prevalent than friction, with recurring alignment around spatial planning, catchment management, and governance tools such as standards, monitoring, regulation, and data sharing. These mechanisms often align land restoration, biodiversity protection, climate action, water governance, and sector delivery in agriculture, fisheries, minerals, and physical planning. At the same time, several cross-cutting frictions are flagged for review where expansion in production, mining, infrastructure, or location-based development may increase pressure on shared land and water systems. The overall picture points to broad strategic alignment, alongside recurring implementation sensitivities in wetlands, watersheds, coastal zones, and other multi-use landscapes.
